newsitem.title: UK: OFTEL estimates BT costs of school plan.
newsitem.headline: OFTEL estimates BT costs of school plan.

text.p: British telecoms watchdog Oftel said on Friday that it estimates the cost that British Telecommunications Plc need to offer internet computer access to UK schools would be around 665 stg per school a year.
Oftel said in a statement that the cost to small primary schools BT would need to offer would be 340 stg per year.
It added the estimates show how low Oftel would allow BT to price down to before prices become anti-competitive.
"These estimates give BT considerable flexibility to develop its original offer to give schools a cheaper deal and longer hours of access," said director general Don Cruickshank.

Oftel wants schools to have access to high speed networks that can support 10-20 computers hooked up to the Internet computer network at any one time, as well as affordable prices and a choice of service provider.
Oftel invited response to the consultative document by August 8, with a second stage for comment on the initial responses until August 22. It is working towards a final conclusion in September.
Oftel has already approved cable company plans to allow schools access to the Internet and some 600-800 schools have signed up under the cable scheme.
